chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Salih ibn Muhammad, from Yaman al-Tammar, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, for the master of this matter there is a disappearance; one who holds fast to his religion during it is like one who plucks the thorns of al-Qatad with his hand. Then he pondered for a while, then said: Indeed, for the master of this matter there is a disappearance, so let a servant of Allah fear Allah and hold fast to his religion. Do not feel desolate in the path of guidance because of the few who follow it.

key_terms.الْمُمْسِكُ بِدِينِهِ: One who holds fast to his religion
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Command (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Imam's description of the occultation and holding fast to religion?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Nu'mani, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) uses the vivid metaphor of placking thorns with bare hands to illustrate the intense spiritual struggle and resilience required to preserve one's faith during the Great Occultation. He further encourages believers not to feel isolated or desolate due to the scarcity of followers, emphasizing that the path of truth is validated by steadfastness rather than numerical majority. This hadith serves as a cornerstone for understanding the psychological and spiritual challenges faced by the Shia community during the prolonged absence of the Imam.
